title: Seventeen Stars Withdrew. Fifteen Seeds Lost in Round One. Four Players Collapsed in the Heat. The 2026 French Open Is the Wildest Grand Slam in a Generation.
excerpt: Alcaraz is absent. Medvedev and Fritz are gone. Djokovic, at thirty-nine, is still standing. And the kid from Andhra Pradesh — Nishesh Basavareddy — pushed his way into the second round before falling. Here is what is happening at Roland Garros.
body:
The 2026 French Open is four days old and already unrecognisable.

Carlos Alcaraz, the defending champion, is not here. A wrist injury sustained at the Barcelona Open in April forced him out of Roland Garros and Wimbledon both. He has been posting from home, watching on television, telling young athletes to embrace uncertainty. The man who won the title last year in a five-set classic against Jannik Sinner will not defend it.

He is not alone. Lorenzo Musetti, ranked eleventh in the world, withdrew. Arthur Fils, the twenty-year-old French hope ranked twentieth, pulled out with a hip injury. Holger Rune, Jack Draper, Sebastian Korda — all gone before the first ball was struck. On the women's side, former Wimbledon champion Marketa Vondrousova withdrew amid a doping charge. In total, twelve players pulled out before the main draw began. Seventeen are now out overall.

## The Heat

Then the heat arrived.

Paris hit thirty-three degrees Celsius on Tuesday — scorching by Parisian standards, dangerous by tennis standards. Four players retired mid-match on a single afternoon. Cameron Norrie, the twentieth seed, stopped while trailing Daniel Vallejo. Alexandre Muller retired against Stefanos Tsitsipas. Sebastian Baez, fighting through a fourth set against Roman Andres Burruchaga, could not continue. Moyuka Uchijima retired against Claire Liu after being unable to recover from a gruelling second set.

In total, six players have retired mid-match across the first three days. The courts are faster than usual, the conditions more brutal. Players are managing ice towels and shade rotations between changeovers. Medvedev's wife, Daria, was caught on camera telling her husband: "It's hot for everybody. Everybody is suffering. You need to behave!"

He did not behave well enough. The fifth seed was stunned by Australian wildcard Adam Walton in five sets.

## The Carnage

Fifteen seeded players lost in the first round. Fifteen. On the men's side: Medvedev (sixth seed), Taylor Fritz (seventh), Alexander Bublik (ninth), Jiri Lehecka (twelfth), Etcheverry (twenty-third), Griekspoor (twenty-ninth), Moutet (thirtieth). It is the first time since 2007 that three top-ten men's seeds have been eliminated before the second round at Roland Garros.

The women's draw was no less brutal. Fifth-seeded Jessica Pegula fell to Australia's Kimberly Birrell. Linda Noskova, Ekaterina Alexandrova, Liudmila Samsonova, Clara Tauson, Leylah Fernandez, and Cristina Bucsa all went out in the opening round.

## The Survivors

At thirty-nine, Novak Djokovic is still here. On Wednesday, he beat France's Valentin Royer in four sets — 6-3, 6-2, 6-7, 6-3 — on Court Philippe Chatrier to reach the third round. He is chasing his twenty-fifth Grand Slam title. With Alcaraz absent and the draw blown open, this might be his best chance in years.

And then there is Jannik Sinner. The world number one has not lost a match on clay all season. He holds a twenty-nine-match winning streak on the surface, has won three consecutive clay-court Masters 1000 titles, and enters Roland Garros as the most overwhelming favourite the tournament has seen in years. Betting markets give him a seventy-four per cent chance of lifting the trophy. No one else is above eight per cent.

## The Diaspora Connection

For Indian tennis fans, this tournament carried hope. Nishesh Basavareddy, a twenty-one-year-old Indian-American whose parents are from Andhra Pradesh, stunned seventh-seeded Taylor Fritz in the first round — 7-6, 7-6, 6-7, 6-1 — in one of the tournament's defining upsets. Fritz later admitted that Basavareddy "cooked me" with his drop shots. It was the kind of performance that earns a player a second look from an entire continent.

His second-round match against compatriot Alex Michelsen, the world number forty-two, was tighter and more punishing. Basavareddy fought hard — winning the third set after dropping the first two — but ultimately fell 6-7, 3-6, 6-3, 3-6. The run is over, but the statement has been made. A player with roots in Telugu-speaking India is now a name on the Grand Slam circuit.

India's other representatives, Yuki Bhambri and N. Sriram Balaji, remain alive in the men's doubles draw. Karman Kaur Thandi, India's highest-ranked women's singles player, was eliminated in the qualifiers.

## What Is Left

The draw is wide open. Alcaraz's absence has removed the one player who could consistently match Sinner on clay. Djokovic, at thirty-nine, has the experience but not the fitness he once did — losing that third set to Royer on Wednesday was a reminder. Felix Auger-Aliassime, Alexander Zverev, and Stefanos Tsitsipas lurk as dark horses, but none of them have been tested the way Sinner has tested himself this season.

For NRIs watching from living rooms in New Jersey and London and Toronto, this French Open is strange and compelling in equal measure. The favourites are falling. The heat is real. The chaos is unprecedented. And somewhere in this disorder, Indian tennis is finding a foothold — one drop shot at a time.

*Sources: Tennis365, InsideSport, Sporting News, WTA Tennis, Polymarket, Sportradar*
